reply: No, the LED NIR kidney study cannot be quoted as proof that your sensor is ready for intra‑operative tumor‑boundary guidance; it was an in‑vitro feasibility study, not an in‑vivo validation. We recommend a staged feasibility plan starting with ex‑vivo tissue samples using a diffuse‑reflection NIR probe and building a calibrated chemometric model before any clinical use.

steps: Collect a representative set of ex‑vivo tissue samples (tumor and normal) from multiple patients.
Measure each sample with the proposed NIR diffuse‑reflection probe and record spectra.
Obtain histopathology reference for each sample to label tumor vs. normal and boundary locations.
Develop a chemometric classification model (PCA/PLS‑DA) using a training subset.
Validate the model on held‑out samples (different patients) to assess accuracy and robustness.
If successful, design a miniaturized in‑vivo probe and repeat steps on fresh surgical specimens.
feasibility.decisionBasis: Feasibility will be confirmed when the ex‑vivo model achieves pre‑agreed classification performance on independent samples and the probe geometry is compatible with the surgical access point.
